key_insight: Superfast cosine and sine transforms extend low-rank tensor-train spectral PDE solvers to homogeneous Neumann and Dirichlet boundary conditions.
engineering_relevance: The framework can reduce solve time and memory requirements for high-resolution convection and computational homogenization simulations.
method: Derive cosine and sine transforms from a shared quantum-circuit-inspired tensor-train operator.
Prove transform ranks are bounded by 6 times the superfast Fourier transform rank at the prescribed accuracy, independently of discretization order.
Apply the transforms to spectral pressure projection and 3D computational homogenization.
evidence_signal: Measured transform ranks plateau near 32 through 2^26 grid points; convection Poisson solves achieve up to 7× speedup at comparable accuracy, while 3D homogenization achieves 2–6× speedup and 4–7× lower memory use against existing TT approaches.
watch_item: The demonstrated boundary-condition extension covers homogeneous Neumann and Dirichlet conditions; performance for more general boundaries remains unestablished.
paper_title: Quantum-Inspired Tensor Train Spectral Solver for High-Resolution PDEs with Non-Periodic Boundary Conditions
